problem.claim: Develop an offline IRL framework that models uncertainty over rewards and full return distributions, enabling distribution-aware policy learning.

gap.claim: Conventional IRL typically estimates deterministic rewards or matches only expected returns, omitting richer distributional structure in expert behavior.

contributions.claim: A distributional offline IRL framework jointly modeling reward-function uncertainty and full return distributions.
An FSD-violation objective that integrates distortion risk measures into policy learning to recover reward distributions and distribution-aware policies.
The authors provide an algorithm with stated O(ε^-2) iteration complexity and report results across synthetic, neurobehavioral, and MuJoCo benchmarks.

stated_novelty.claim: The authors distinguish their approach from conventional IRL by jointly recovering reward distributions and distribution-aware policies rather than deterministic rewards or expected returns alone.

author_reported_evidence.claim: The authors report convergence with O(ε^-2) iteration complexity.
The authors report expressive reward representations and state-of-the-art imitation performance on synthetic benchmarks, real-world neurobehavioral data, and MuJoCo control tasks.

narrative_sequence.summary: Introduces an offline IRL framework for uncertainty over rewards and full return distributions.
Contrasts the framework with deterministic-reward and expected-return methods, using FSD violations and DRMs to learn distribution-aware policies.
Positions the formulation for behavior analysis and risk-aware imitation learning.
States an iteration-complexity result, then reports benchmark results spanning synthetic, neurobehavioral, and MuJoCo settings.

source_observation.claim: The abstract pairs a specific modeling distinction—reward and return distributions—with a matching optimization mechanism based on FSD violations and DRMs.

lessons.interpretation: A compact abstract can make a methodological claim more interpretable by linking what is modeled to how it is optimized.
lessons.application: When presenting a new distributional or uncertainty-aware method, explicitly map each richer object being modeled to the loss or constraint that operationalizes it.
lessons.exception: This framing is less suitable when the method's key contribution is primarily theoretical, architectural, or resource-oriented rather than an altered modeled quantity.

unknowns: The convergence statement omits assumptions, the precise algorithm, and what ε measures.
The reported state-of-the-art comparison does not identify baselines, metrics, statistical details, or whether all tasks use the same evaluation protocol.
The abstract does not quantify reward-representation or imitation improvements, nor specify how risk measures are selected.
